python.sorted.description: Returns a new sorted list from the items in an iterable.

attributes.name: reverse
attributes.description: When true, sorts the result in descending order.

returns.name: list
returns.description: A new list containing the sorted values.

behavioralNotes: Does not modify the original iterable
Useful when you need to preserve the original order

explanations.text: The original list starts in unsorted order.
sorted creates a new list instead of changing items.

output: Use list.sort() when you intentionally want in-place sorting.

python.len.description: Returns the number of items in a container.

attributes.name: obj
attributes.description: The container or sequence to measure.

returns.name: int
returns.description: The number of items in the object.

behavioralNotes: Does not modify the input object
Usually runs in constant time for built-in containers

explanations.text: len reads the container size and returns it as an integer.

output: len reports size; it does not inspect or transform the contents.
